Actual macOS VM lifecycle — audits2270,1875 and the VM subset of2060

Existing runner only
--------------------
Not registered in hosted CI. Its only hosted execution (macos-15-intel, TCG,
https://github.com/wendylabsinc/WendyOS/actions/runs/43593970058/job/132444620222)
passed cancellation, then the guest was still starting its container runtime
when the production 5-minute simulator wait expired. Run it on the reserved
ARM64/HVF Mac, after an actual CLI Make build and commands install.test compilation. Inspect command -v qemu-system-aarch64 and its --version first; install
Homebrew qemu only if absent in this disposable job. Its native binary and
64MiB edk2-aarch64-code.fd are recorded by SHA256 and version at execution.
No host networking, hypervisor, service, or kernel configuration is changed.

python3 .github/scripts/test-macos-vm-lifecycle.py \
  --cli "$ACTUAL_MAKE_CLI" --test-binary "$EXISTING_COMMANDS_TEST" \
  --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-vm-lifecycle"

Use the job's actual paths, not another compile of the normal commands suite.
The binary must include TestVMOwnedLifecycle from this source; missing/skipped
selection cannot pass. The wrapper builds one static Linux/ARM64 guest app and
one source-overlay forwarding control using the existing Go cache. Set the
existing step timeout to35min and existing job timeout to45min (no added row).
The wrapper's total32min deadline includes both phases; normal14min/control8min
are upper bounds, not measured runtime. The outer job budget includes dependency
setup and its other tests. Reduce bounds only after actual hosted measurements.
It requires12GiB free before staging one pinned606MB compressed released guest
and sequential16GiB sparse VM disks. The exact release bmap reports
7,383,041,024 expanded bytes (metadata SHA256
cc80175c46ef843763ca76bf02a936af34a4521a7e616c6c6e24d2af2a164dcb,
https://storage.googleapis.com/wendyos-images-public/images/vm-arm64/0.21.0/wendyos-image-vm-arm64-wendyos.rootfs.wic.bmap).
The remainder covers the compressed archive, small app/build outputs and guest
writes; the control begins only after the normal disk is removed. No cold VM/image download was run locally.
Always retain output/*.log and output/*.json; no disk/binary/media artifacts.
Register macos_vm_lifecycle_test.py in existing portable automation tests.

Actual assertions
-----------------
The published vm-arm64 0.21.0 bytes/size/SHA are shared with the Windows fixture.
Actual CLI vm create writes a fresh private configuration/disk. Production
ensureSimulatorRunning starts detached QEMU; the fixture's private QMP socket
pauses its CPU before readiness, verifies the actual Agent cannot answer, and
cancels discover's exact startSimulatorFn wait. The same QEMU/runstate must remain
alive. QMP resume plus the same production callback must reach the real Agent.
No launcher, transport, QMP, Agent, or forwarding fake is installed.

A source-built static ARM64 ELF is packaged as a scratch OCI image and sent
through production chunk upload/PrepareImage/RunContainer. Host port must be
closed before forwarding. Actual prepareVMAppPorts and readiness/hook address
resolution are called twice, then HTTP must return this run's nonce, a live
guest boot_id, and increasing counters. Production QMP powerdown must release
the inherited run lock and refuse further HTTP. Starting the same VM disk/alias
must preserve the owned regular disk inode, Agent hostname and agent port, produce a new guest boot_id,
start the persisted restart=no app without reupload, and restore actual forwarded HTTP.

The historical forwarding control removes only prepareVMAppPorts' call to
forwardVMPorts (the missing behavior fixed by0a3c57ff89c6c8e). It must fail at the
named actual application readiness boundary after real boot/upload/start; a
compile/setup/boot failure, timeout, skip, or unknown cleanup cannot pass.

Ownership and result scope
--------------------------
Every phase has a fresh short /tmp/wv-* private root, nonce-bound VM name and
configuration, file-only credentials, and no Cloud enrollment/registration.
No existing user VM or user Keychain is read. The guardian bounds ordinary
subprocesses. Detached QEMU owns a new process session, so cleanup separately
uses only that private QMP socket and waits for its actual inherited flock to
release. It never signals a saved PID. Unknown QMP/drain retains the owned work
and fails; logs report its exact path for the owner. No recursive work deletion
occurs while QEMU may still write the disk. A job cancellation should still allow
the35min step's cleanup margin; if a forced runner termination interrupts it,
only the disposable runner is discarded, never claim observed clean drain.

This closes no UI/picker rendering, Cloud enrollment, Windows unsupported
background/QMP behavior, nested ARM64 host, or physical Mac claim.2060 is a
mixed audit: its other mapped protocol/runtime evidence remains separate.
Hosted execution is pending until all normal/control markers and evidence pass.

GetAgentVersion on the shipped Go Agent does not populate PublicKey. This
fixture therefore makes no cryptographic guest-identity claim: it verifies the
actual hostname, owned disk inode/runstate/port, QMP ownership and fresh
nonce-bound application bytes across a changed guest boot_id.
